by_doi.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>The composition of plant cell walls is important in determining cereal end uses. Unlike other widely consumed cereal grains barley is comparatively rich in (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan, a source of dietary fibre. Previous work showed <jats:italic>Cellulose synthase-like</jats:italic> genes synthesise (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan in several tissues. <jats:italic>HvCslF6</jats:italic> encodes a grain (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan synthase, whereas the function of <jats:italic>HvCslF9</jats:italic> is unknown. Here, the relationship between mRNA levels of <jats:italic>HvCslF6</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>HvCslF9</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>HvGlbI</jats:italic> (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan endohydrolase, and (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan content was studied in developing grains of four barley cultivars. <jats:italic>HvCslF6</jats:italic> was differentially expressed during mid (8–15 DPA) and late (38 DPA) grain development stages while <jats:italic>HvCslF9</jats:italic> transcript was only clearly detected at 8–10 DPA. A peak of <jats:italic>HvGlbI</jats:italic> expression was detected at 15 DPA. Differences in transcript abundance across the three genes could partially explain variation in grain (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan content in these genotypes. Remarkably narrow sequence variation was found within the <jats:italic>HvCslF6</jats:italic> promoter and coding sequence and does not explain variation in (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan content. Our data emphasise the genotype-dependent accumulation of (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan during barley grain development and a role for the balance between hydrolysis and synthesis in determining (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan content, and suggests that other regulatory sequences or proteins are likely to be involved in this trait in developing grain.</jats:p>
title: Barley grain (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan content: effects of transcript and sequence variation in genes encoding the corresponding synthase and endohydrolase enzymes

title: Intermediate resolution structure of barley (1,3;1,4)-beta-glucan synthase CslF6.

search.abstract: <jats:p>Mixed linkage (1,3;1,4)-β-glucan (MLG) is a major non-cellulosic polysaccharide of commelinid monocot cell walls and an important soluble dietary fibre component found in cereal grains, including those of barley. Despite its importance, relatively little is known about the regulation of cellulose synthase-like F6 (CSLF6), the major MLG synthase (MLGS) isoform involved in MLG biosynthesis in developing grain and young vegetative tissues. We investigated potential post-transcriptional regulation of CSLF6 using complementary protein complex, co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP), and biochemical approaches. Higher-order CSLF6-containing complexes were detected under non-denaturing conditions. Co-IP using detergent-solubilised barley microsomal membranes (MM) identified 16 Class I and 37 Class II candidate CSLF6-associated proteins. Biochemical analyses of in vitro MLGS activity in 4-day-old barley seedling MMs, as a proxy for CSLF6 activity, indicated that alkaline pH in the presence of Mg2+ and Ca2+ enhanced MLGS activity. A soluble protein fraction (>100,000 g supernatant) from barley seedlings, lacking CSLF6, stimulated MLGS activity when combined with MM, supporting the presence of one or more soluble proteinaceous stimulatory factors. The combination of size-exclusion chromatography, MLGS activity assays and comparative mass spectrometry identified proteins enriched in this active protein fraction, including candidates associated with signalling/regulation and protein modification or turnover. The soluble fraction also stimulated MLGS activity in wheat and ryegrass microsomal membrane (MM) preparations, suggesting that the stimulatory activity may involve a conserved component of the MLGS machinery. Together, these findings identify candidate CSLF6-associated proteins and soluble proteinaceous factors that may contribute to MLGS regulation and provide targets for functional validation.</jats:p>
